question: What filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose for host-mode agents: a `tools.fs` allow/deny PathGuard policy, a `tools.fs.roots` access-mode policy, a narrower workspace-only/exec-split design, or no core host path ACL beyond sandboxing?
rationale: This defines a public config and security boundary, affects existing operator workflows, and has competing open implementation designs with different compatibility and false-security tradeoffs.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
options.body: Choose a canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging either implementation path.

options.title: Split exec into a separate security tracker
options.body: Allow a file-tool-only policy only if docs, labels, and follow-up tracking clearly state shell-mediated filesystem access remains outside that boundary.

options.title: Defer to OS or container isolation
options.body: Reject core host path ACLs if maintainers decide workspaceOnly plus sandbox backends are the intended boundary, then close related implementation PRs with that policy.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Choose a canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging either implementation path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced and refactored the current workspace-only guard and already framed the prior maintainer-side review for this canonical issue.
